title: Machine learning-enabled spatial multi-omics uncovers lactate-driven targets and tumor microenvironmental reprogramming in cancer.
summary: Integrated spatial and single-cell multi-omics with machine-learning analyses found different cell-type patterns in high- and low-lactate lung adenocarcinoma samples, with selected programs associated with survival. Spatial metabolomics and immunofluorescence provide supporting measurements; these are observational associations and do not establish lactate as a causal driver or therapeutic target.
ai_technology: Machine-learning analysis integrates spatial, single-cell, and molecular measurements to identify tumor-microenvironment associations.
organization: Zhuzhou Hospital, Central South University; Tumor ImmunoMetabolism Institute, Zhuzhou Hospital

evidence.tested: High-lactate samples showed greater epithelial and fibroblast abundance, while low-lactate samples had more T/NK cells and monocytes/macrophages; selected programs associated with survival.
evidence.unknown: Spatial measurements and survival associations are observational; no causal lactate effect or therapeutic benefit is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning integration prioritized cell-type and molecular associations linked to lactate states and clinical outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
